A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Mufu research. Their text, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching content across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original FLORES-200 and NTREX translation experiments, including fine-tuning, distillation, ablations, and attention analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and reports additional PaLM2 S, LoRA, auxiliary-language ablation, and BLEU results.

M1.justification: Section 4.3 adds rank-16 LoRA fine-tuning of PaLM2 S, changing which parameters are updated. The core multilingual postediting and sequence-distillation procedures remain unchanged; using the same teacher and student model was already permitted in v1.

E1.justification: FLORES-200 training and evaluation over 201 translation directions, NTREX evaluation over 112 languages, and the NTL and distillation data sources are retained. Added experiments change model configurations, auxiliary-candidate composition, and metrics within existing coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds a qualitative comparison using five-shot PaLM2 XXS–NTL without parameter updates, reported worse than baseline fine-tuning in footnote 11. The PaLM2 S teacher and NLLB 1.3B distilled and 54B benchmark comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds BLEU evaluation, PaLM2 S student experiments, LoRA settings, and controls with 25 auxiliary candidates. Appendix A.3 refines the reported checkpoint criterion to validation chrF for very-low- and low-resource languages, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. The original data splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds tests of using the same teacher and student, model-size-related overfitting, and LoRA versus full fine-tuning. It extends the high-resource-only and postediting-removal ablations to Gemma 7B and tests adding five high-resource candidates to mufu20. Existing attention analyses and failure examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% confidence intervals across language pairs in Figure 2. V2 applies the same practice to additional models and its BLEU figure, without adding repeated-run counts, seeds, or statistical testing procedures.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds model and ablation results, including PaLM2 S LoRA scores of 47.2 chrF on FLORES-200 and 50.1 on NTREX. V2 adds BLEU results and revises BLOOMZ scores: FLORES baseline changes from 27.4 to 28.0 and mufu10 from 41.2 to 41.0. BLOOMZ's removed five-epoch statement prevents confirming identical training conditions. Retained main-table rows and the 201-language results table otherwise match.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces formal theorems, proofs, or derivations. V2's clearer explanation of win percentages restates the existing metric rather than changing its mathematical definition.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same method, data-efficiency, low-resource performance, and distillation claims, including the 64% NLLB win rate and 3.1 chrF improvement. The central multilingual-reasoning conclusion is unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning overfitting, LoRA's knowledge-retention versus new-skill tradeoff, and difficulties improving strong teacher translations using human references. It discusses model-dependent effects of additional high-resource candidates and quantifies the inference-cost tradeoff in Section 6. The original alignment explanation and failure conditions remain.

D1.justification: V2 documents LoRA rank, handling overlaps to obtain 25 distinct auxiliary candidates, and the low-resource checkpoint-selection criterion. It removes the NLLB 54B translation-source link, the NLLB 1.3B default-decoding note, and BLOOMZ's explicit five-epoch description. A replacement BLOOMZ-specific budget is not stated.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for BLEU, LoRA, adaptation-related forgetting, and differences between human and model translations, including Papineni, Hu, Biderman, Sizov, Zhang, and Kocmi. Its positioning relative to in-context learning, multilingual reasoning, and low-resource translation remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized prose revisions, expands Section 4.3, reorders part of related work, adds acknowledgments and a BLEU appendix subsection, and corrects cross-references. The introduction, method narrative, and most existing appendix explanations remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains model and ablation rows, while Figure 2 adds PaLM2 S and LoRA with adjusted axes and legends. New BLEU Tables 6–7 and Figure 4 reuse existing comparison formats. Table 3 and appendix material are reflowed or renumbered; the method diagram and attention examples are retained.

improvement.justification: The BLEU checks and targeted ablations strengthen empirical support and clarify tuning and auxiliary-context tradeoffs; the cost discussion is more concrete. These gains are tempered by removed reproducibility details and an unrevised ablation interpretation: new Gemma 7B results show mufu5tr below postediting alone, 42.9 versus 46.3 FLORES chrF, contrary to Section 4.3's general statement. Overall, the additions provide a limited net quality improvement.
